skill_title: Identify taxable income and use a tax deduction table
notes: 20-item bank, Grade 12 only. CAPS mix: 10 L1 / 10 L2. Read payslip to find taxable income. Use a SARS-style tax deduction table to look up monthly PAYE.

stimulus.inline: Gross pay = basic + allowances. Taxable income = Gross − pre-tax deductions (e.g. pension).

items.question: Gross R20 000, pension contribution R1 500. Calculate taxable income.

stimulus.inline:
**SARS monthly PAYE deduction table (simplified, illustrative)**

| Monthly taxable income (R) | Monthly PAYE (R) |
|---|---|
| 10 000 | 510 |
| 12 000 | 870 |
| 15 000 | 1 540 |
| 18 000 | 2 220 |
| 20 000 | 2 670 |
| 25 000 | 3 920 |

items.question: Look up the monthly PAYE for taxable income R15 000.
workingSteps: Read the table row for R15 000 → R1 540.

stimulus.inline: UIF is calculated separately at 1% of gross (capped). Not deducted before tax.

items.question: Does UIF reduce taxable income (yes/no)?
workingSteps: UIF is calculated separately on gross; it does NOT reduce taxable income.

stimulus.inline: Net pay = Gross − (PAYE + UIF + pension + other deductions). Payslip: Gross R20 000, PAYE R2 670, UIF R177,12 (capped), pension R1 600.

items.question: Calculate net pay.

stimulus.inline: Pre-tax deductions reduce taxable income; post-tax deductions don't.

items.question: Is 'medical aid contribution' typically a PRE-TAX deduction?
options: No — medical aid is usually post-tax.
items.expectedAnswer: No — medical aid is usually post-tax.
workingSteps: In SA, medical aid contribution is post-tax (a medical-aid TAX CREDIT is then applied separately).

_error_signal_vocabulary.ERR_TAXABLE_INCOME: Includes/excludes the wrong items when calculating taxable income.
_error_signal_vocabulary.ERR_TABLE_LOOKUP: Reads the wrong row from a tax table.
_error_signal_vocabulary.ERR_GROSS_VS_BASIC: Confuses basic salary with gross pay.
_error_signal_vocabulary.ERR_INTERPOLATION: Linear interpolation between table rows is incorrect.
_error_signal_vocabulary.ERR_PERCENT_BASE_INVERTED: Uses the wrong base when finding PAYE % of gross.
